title: Sales enablement playbook — positioning, messaging, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Morgan Lee
content:
Executive summary

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core sales enablement assets for field sellers and solution engineers: concise positioning and messaging, competitor brief summaries and win themes, a recommended pitch deck outline and demo checklist, pricing guidance and discount guardrails, representative case studies, and a security FAQ for prospects. Use this as the single source of truth for pre-sales motion and customer-facing collateral.

Owners & scope
- Document owner: go-to-market (sales enablement)
- Contributors: product, engineering, security, finance
- Audience: AEs, SDRs, SEs, solutions architects, partner sellers
- Scope: Enterprise and mid-market opportunities where inference economics, reliability, and deployment flexibility are primary buying criteria

1) Positioning & messaging (elevator -> value props -> proof points)

Elevator pitch (15-30s):
Redwood Inference delivers predictable, production-grade LLM inference that optimizes latency, cost, and reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—so engineering teams can ship LLM features without building and operating complex serving infrastructure.

Primary value propositions (short bullets for slide/opener):
- Production-first performance: industry-leading latency and throughput controls backed by observability and SLOs
- Unified runtime across environments: same API and tooling for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
- Cost-aware controls: batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations to reduce unit economics without sacrificing quality
- Enterprise-ready: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and Private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging

Supporting proof points and metrics (use in pitch/decks):
- Typical latency: 50-150 ms p50 for common 1k-token generation flows on curated models (customer benchmarks vary)
- Cost reduction levers: customers commonly achieve 2-5x reductions in per-token cost via batching + caching + quantization profiles
- Reliability: multi-tier routing + automatic fallback reduces production failures by ~90% in our internal canary tests
- Case study highlights: Fortune 100 fintech reduced inference TCO by 42% and improved 99th percentile latency by 36% after migration

Segmentation & tailored messaging
- AI-native startups: emphasize rapid time-to-value, self-serve API, and cost controls to scale usage
- Mid-market product teams: focus on predictable capacity (Dedicated), cost forecasting, and observability
- Regulated/enterprise: emphasize Private deployment, network isolation (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM, compliance evidence and audit logs

2) Competitive landscape & briefings (one-pagers for reps)

Competitor snapshot (top themes):
- General cloud AI endpoints: good for quick prototype; limited cost controls and may lack multi-environment consistency
- LLM API-focused vendors: simple APIs but often trade off performance transparency and enterprise deployment modes
- Self-hosted inference runtimes: offer deep control but require significant engineering investment to achieve production reliability and autoscaling

Win themes vs. common competitors (use as rebuttal bullets):
- vs cloud AI endpoints: "We provide the same developer ergonomics plus predictable economics and enterprise deployment options—no re-architecture required when you scale."
- vs API-first LLM vendors: "Comparable ease-of-use with stronger observability, SLOs, and routing/fallback policies for production reliability."
- vs self-hosted runtimes: "We deliver curated, validated runtime profiles and managed options that remove the heavy maintenance burden while preserving control via Private deployments."

Differentiation matrix (talk track, not slide table):
- Developer ergonomics: parity with API providers
- Production economics: superior (batching/caching/quantization tooling + per-route cost breakdowns)
- Deployment flexibility: unique (hosted / dedicated / private)
- Enterprise controls: robust (SLA, KMS/HSM, audit logs, VPC/private control plane)

3) Pitch deck & demo guidance (recommended structure + talk track)

Recommended pitch deck outline (10-12 slides):
1. Title & hook (customer pain: unpredictable latency/cost/reliability)
2. Market context (LLM adoption, risk of re-architecting infra)
3. Redwood in one line + 3 bullet differentiators
4. How it works (runtime, smart routing, caching, deployment modes)
5. Key capabilities: latency SLOs, batching/caching, observability, rollouts
6. Deployment options & security controls (SLA, Private, KMS, audit)
7. Pricing & economic model (high-level tiers and example math)
8. Case study (impact numbers)
9. Implementation and timeline (POC -> pilot -> production)
10. Support & SLA summary
11. Next steps & recommended technical contacts

Demo checklist (SE playbook):
- Prep: confirm attendee roles and a short list of customer use cases
- Live demo sequence:
  1) Quick API call (1-2 minutes) to show developer ergonomics
  2) Dashboard walkthrough: per-route latency/cost breakdowns, traces, rollout controls
  3) Show routing/fallback policy in action: simulate a capacity constraint and failover to compatible model
  4) Show Dedicated capacity config and Private deployment options (VPC, KMS)
- Performance micro-demo: run two short generation flows showing p50 and p95 for same model with and without batching/cache enabled
- Security/data controls mini-demo: show audit logs, RBAC, and KMS key integration (sanitized examples)

4) Pricing guidance & playbook for discounts

Pricing tiers (high-level):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing and per-embedding pricing; best for rapid prototyping and smaller teams
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commits for predictable throughput and cost; recommended for sustained high QPS
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + support tier + optional on-prem packaging; recommended when data residency or heavy compliance is required

Recommended pricing conversation flow:
1. Establish expected volume (tokens/month), peak concurrency, and latency SLO needs
2. Show cost math for hosted vs dedicated vs private with example scenarios
3. Recommend POC scope: 2-4 week pilot on hosted or dedicated depending on scale

Discount and contracting guardrails:
- Standard discounts apply for 12/24 month committed spend; finance must approve any >30% discount off list pricing
- Technical discount levers: encourage customers to adopt batching, caching, and quantization to reduce unit costs rather than deep headline discounts
- Commercial concessions: for strategic deals, combine modest price concessions with implementation credits, prioritized onboarding, and extended SLA terms

5) Case studies & talking points (use in slides and emails)

1) Fintech (Tier 1 bank) - Use case: real-time risk summarization and customer support routing
- Challenge: inconsistent latency under burst loads and increasing inference TCO
- Solution: Dedicated capacity + prefix caching and optimized quantization profile
- Outcome: 42% reduction in inference TCO, 36% improvement in p99 latency, and 2-week migration timeline with no customer-facing incidents
- Quote: "Redwood let us move to production without hiring a separate infra team." — Head of Data Engineering

2) SaaS marketplace - Use case: search relevancy and personalized recommendations
- Challenge: high cost per query and unpredictable tail latency across regions
- Solution: Multi-region routing, KV cache for popular prefixes, and per-route autoscaling rules
- Outcome: 3x throughput at 60% lower per-query cost during peak events; integrated rollout reduced regressions by 80%

6) Security FAQ for prospects (top questions SEs will get)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: For Hosted deployments, data resides in the cloud region selected by the customer with optional regional restrictions; Dedicated provides tenant isolation; Private gives full control (VPC/on-prem). We publish region availability and data residency options in the onboarding doc.

Q: How is sensitive data protected in transit and at rest?
A: All customer traffic uses TLS 1.2+/mTLS for service-to-service; data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS when configured (Private + Dedicated integration). Audit logs are tamper-evident and available via the console and syslog/S3/SIEM integrations.

Q: Do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK)?
A: Yes. KMS/HSM integrations are available for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we provide interop with cloud KMS for key rotation.

Q: How do you prevent model leakage or data retention issues?
A: We provide configurable retention windows, selective logging, and redaction rules. Private deployments can be air-gapped or deployed on-prem to meet strict non-exfiltration requirements.

Q: What compliance frameworks do you support?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II, and provide evidence packages for enterprise audits; roadmap includes additional industry attestations as required per customer. Work with security team for customer-specific questionnaires (we maintain an FAQ and RFP library).

Q: How is customer metadata and telemetry secured?
A: Telemetry is segregated by tenant; role-based access controls (RBAC) limit console and API access. We provide log forwarding and can integrate with customer SIEMs for centralized monitoring.

7) Implementation & pilot plan (recommended engagement pattern)

POC / Pilot (4-6 weeks recommended):
- Week 0: Kickoff, success criteria, stakeholder alignment
- Week 1-2: Integration and baseline benchmarking (use customer prompts + traffic profile)
- Week 3: Optimization (batching/caching/quantization tuning and routing policies)
- Week 4: Pilot validation, ROI deck, and production readiness runbook

Production rollout checklist:
- Model pinning & version control established
- Rollout policy (canary/A-B/fallback) configured
- Observability dashboards and alerting in place (latency, error rates, cost per route)
- SLA and escalation contact documented

9) Next steps & cadence
- For new logo pursuit: run this playbook during pre-sales alignment call; schedule SE demo with focused use case within 72 hours of discovery call
- Quarterly refresh: sales enablement will update this playbook after each major product release and after two enterprise wins/losses

Appendix: quick rebuttal snippets (copy/paste for emails)
- "If you're worried about re-architecture: Redwood offers a Private deployment path and curated runtime profiles so you can adopt incrementally without a forklift migration."
- "If cost is the blocker: we'll run a baseline benchmark and show expected unit economics with batching/caching enabled before you sign anything."
